cards.title: AEO mental model: execute like Google, measure like Facebook
cards.summary: Treat answer-engine optimization as SEO-style content work but measure it with ad-style attribution (view-through, self-reported) rather than click-through, because AI referrals are invisible to analytics.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to resource and measure an AEO/generative-search channel for your store, when direct referrer traffic looks flat or falling but you suspect AI assistants are driving discovery.
steps: Execute the channel as you would Google SEO: publish thorough, intent-matched content on your own site and the third-party surfaces LLMs read, targeting the prompts and phrases buyers actually type.
Do NOT judge the channel by Google Analytics click-through referrals alone; analytics cannot see most AI-driven discovery because users never click through.

Add a self-reported attribution survey at signup/checkout ('How did you hear about us?') with AI assistants surfaced as explicit options rather than buried under 'Other'. In the source's experience, moving this question to the front and naming the AI options sharply increased responses.

Track both curves separately: click-through referrals (can fall) and self-reported mentions (can rise simultaneously). Gamma saw ChatGPT-referred traffic grow roughly 8x across channels while click-through later declined.
Accept the measurement is analogous to Facebook view-through attribution: imperfect, but the best available proxy until platform-level reporting exists.
caveats: Source is a growth lead's heuristic account at one large consumer SaaS company, not an audited benchmark; the 8x figure is a case example, not a promise.
Self-reported data is noisy and subject to recall bias.
cards.source_name: The Head of Growth at a $100M Company Explains AEO.docx

cards.title: Platform-by-platform AEO playbooks diverge: don't run one strategy
cards.summary: Reddit's influence is largely isolated to ChatGPT, and the playbooks for ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Gemini and Google AI Overviews differ substantially.
cards.use_when: Allocating limited content and community effort across AI surfaces that send or influence traffic to your store (e.g., deciding whether a Reddit push will help Perplexity visibility).
steps: Rank platforms by influence for your product type before investing. Source ranking for consumer/prosumer: (1) ChatGPT, (2) own website, (3) other people's websites (blogs, PR, reviews), (4) YouTube, (5) LinkedIn.
Treat Reddit as primarily a ChatGPT lever (they have a data deal); it will not lift Perplexity or Claude the same way.
Expect roughly 30-40% overlap across the four engines (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews) per the source's observations, leaving ~60% requiring engine-specific work.
For Google AI Overviews, play by SEO rules: strong SEO is effectively good AEO in the whole Google context.
For Perplexity, weight third-party authority sources more heavily.
For Claude, pursue the ecosystem route (MCP server listing) rather than expecting citation-driven acquisition.
caveats: Overlap figure is a stated heuristic observation, not a measurement.
Reddit's ChatGPT data deal and platform mechanics may change; verify current behavior.
cards.source_name: The Head of Growth at a $100M Company Explains AEO.docx

cards.title: Prioritize AI surfaces differently for prosumer vs enterprise buyers
cards.summary: Consumer/prosumer discovery concentrates heavily in ChatGPT, while enterprise-tool research happens in Claude and Copilot, so platform priority should flip by segment.
cards.use_when: Choosing which AI assistant to optimize for when launching or repositioning a product aimed at either individual buyers or enterprise buyers.
steps: For prosumer/consumer products, prioritize: (1) ChatGPT, (2) Google AI Overviews (double benefit from SEO distribution), (3) Perplexity, (4) Claude. The source reports 90%+ of its AI-driven acquisition comes from ChatGPT because everyday users default to it.

For enterprise, flip the ranking: (1) Claude (buyers query tools while working in it daily), (2) Copilot/Bing (source reports meaningful traffic under the Bing umbrella, with distribution advantages from large companies), then ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity.
Note Claude helps retention/extension of existing users more than new-customer acquisition per the source, because Claude cites far less (~5x less than ChatGPT, per studies cited).
caveats: Rankings are the source's heuristic bets for a consumer SaaS, presented as educated guesses, not measured benchmarks.
Claude citation-rate comparison is attributed to third-party studies referenced in the conversation, not independently verified here.
cards.source_name: The Head of Growth at a $100M Company Explains AEO.docx

cards.title: Treat Claude as a Play Store, not a search engine: build an MCP server
cards.summary: Claude's low citation rate makes ecosystem integration via MCP servers the viable route; the source predicts Claude becomes app-store-like while ChatGPT stays search-like.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to invest engineering time in an MCP server or integration listing to get recommended inside an AI assistant's workflow.
steps: Build and list an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server so users can connect your product inside Claude; the source frames this as the primary way to be present and recommended in Anthropic's ecosystem.
Make setup frictionless: remote installation via pasted link with OAuth is now possible versus earlier zip-file local installs (verify the current interface, as this is evolving quickly).
Recognize the current constraint: hosting an MCP alone does not generate discovery — you still must drive users to connect it (marketing/education), unlike an app store that surfaces you.
Expect the model to evolve toward a store where users natively search for apps, creating openings for mobile-native-style products.
Keep an MCP for products you already sell as a low-cost presence play; source suggests building one even just to be picked up in the ecosystem.
caveats: MCP tooling and Anthropic review requirements change fast — verify current listing and install flows.
Source calls this a slow route; citations and discovery benefits are unproven.
This is the source's thesis/quasi-prediction, not a demonstrated result.
cards.source_name: The Head of Growth at a $100M Company Explains AEO.docx

cards.title: Reddit playbook: open-ecosystem wedge posts and competitor-comparison framing
cards.summary: Succeed on Reddit by posting value-oriented content that leverages your tool's interoperability and explicit competitor comparisons, and avoid brand-only self-promotion.
cards.use_when: Planning Reddit participation to earn ChatGPT citations and reach buyers in relevant subreddits without posts being removed.
steps: Pick subreddits via two lenses: (a) ICP lens — where your buyer persona congregates (e.g., a SaaS or marketing subreddit), and (b) problem-universe lens — where your product category is discussed (e.g., a PowerPoint or Canva subreddit for a presentation tool).

Write posts around your product's open ecosystem: if users can import from or export to an adjacent tool, you can contribute authentically in that tool's community (e.g., 'made this in X tool, exported to PowerPoint').
Frame content as comparisons: 'how is our tool better than [competitor]' or 'vs' posts get picked up; pure 'our product is great' posts do not.
Choose deliberately which competitors to be compared against — you implicitly promote whoever you name, so select ones favorable to your positioning and avoid amplifying dangerous rivals.
Niche down aggressively: 'best CRM for health tech sales people' beats 'best CRM for healthcare' beats 'best CRM' for reducing competition — same as the SEO long-tail playbook.
caveats: Comments are for sentiment, not discovery lift: the source sees no meaningful impact from commenting on citation direction.
Negative sentiment can get indexed and persist for months, per a referenced case; the claim that LLMs bias toward negative content is a stated theory, not established fact.
Don't over-focus on tiny subreddits at scale — source says these won't move a large company, though they may matter for small startups or niche topics.
cards.source_name: The Head of Growth at a $100M Company Explains AEO.docx

cards.title: Reddit citation timing: 30-45 day lag on ChatGPT, next-day on Perplexity
cards.summary: New Reddit content takes roughly 30-45 days to be cited by ChatGPT but can be cited by Perplexity as fast as the next day, informing how early to seed content.
cards.use_when: Timing Reddit or community content pushes ahead of a product launch or seasonal campaign when you need citations live by a specific date.
steps: Seed Reddit content at least 30-45 days before you need ChatGPT citations, based on the source's observed lag for new content.
For Perplexity-targeted queries, content can be picked up much faster (next day), especially for specific niche prompt phrases.
For Google AI Overviews, source reports one observed same-day pickup from a niche query — timing is getting faster but varies.
Prioritize participation in other people's subreddits early when starting out; build your own subreddit for the long term (own-community content is cited later).

Plan for citation half-life: the source theorizes citations expire on a cycle and must be refreshed (they manually track citation share in a spreadsheet), so treat Reddit as an always-on engine, not a one-time push.
caveats: Timing figures are observational from one company's experience, not guaranteed SLAs.
Citation lifetime/half-life is explicitly the source's untested hypothesis.
cards.source_name: The Head of Growth at a $100M Company Explains AEO.docx

cards.title: AEO 80/20 rule: optimize primarily for crawlers, keep it human-digestible
cards.summary: For AEO-designated initiatives, allocate roughly 80% of effort to agent/crawler consumption and 20% to human readability so content still makes sense if a human finds it.
cards.use_when: Producing YouTube videos, LinkedIn content, or blog posts with the explicit intent of earning AI citations rather than direct human clicks.
steps: Label the initiative as AEO-first and design around agent consumption: choose titles, headings and structure from prompts/phrases people type, not clickbait headlines designed for human clicks.
Keep ~20% human-oriented so a person landing on it isn't alienated — it should still be digestible and coherent to a reader.

Decide content angle deliberately: don't just describe the product ('this is a glass of water'); go deeper into comparative/meaningful angles ('why is this steel glass better than plastic') and avoid thin, keyword-stuffed repetition.
Push back on the assumption that AI-written content must be spam: modern models can produce well-researched, thick content, and LLMs are more likely to reward depth.
Accept that this is consciously 'gaming' the engine under game-theory pressure — the advantage erodes once platforms detect and close it.
caveats: The 80/20 split is the source's rule of thumb, not a measured optimum.
Source acknowledges gaming carries reputational/durability risk and expects platforms to penalize it (e.g., a referenced Google search update penalized low-value content sites).
cards.source_name: The Head of Growth at a $100M Company Explains AEO.docx

cards.title: Compete in AI citation by niching down the prompt, then expanding
cards.summary: You cannot win broad AI queries like 'best CRM', so start with narrow, defensible prompt phrasings, build topical authority, then attempt broader terms.
cards.use_when: Targeting AI-assistant answers in a crowded product category where broad 'best X' queries are dominated by incumbents.
steps: Map the query landscape from broad to narrow: 'best CRM' → 'best CRM for SMB' → 'best CRM for fintech' → 'best CRM for health tech sales people'.
Enter at the narrow end where competition is lowest and you can plausibly be cited.
Build topical authority/relevance at that niche level first, then take another shot at broader terms.
On Reddit specifically, use the same strategy: rather than a generic post, target the niche comparison where you can place favorable and get cited.
Expect competitors to follow you into niches — when they do, keep moving to the next under-served angle; the source frames 'keep moving' as what growth is.
Treat this as an always-on engine: continuously produce and refresh content, since you cannot rely on a one-time citation.
caveats: This is the source's stated approach; they explicitly say they lack a proven formula for citation lifetime or selection logic.
No guaranteed ranking — success depends on category and competition.
cards.source_name: The Head of Growth at a $100M Company Explains AEO.docx

cards.title: AEO channel priority and citation-lifetime tracking
cards.summary: Own-site content is cited fastest and most controllably; track citation share manually to detect when citations expire.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to publish before your own site versus third-party channels, and setting up a lightweight system to monitor AI citation retention.
steps: Prioritize your own website content: source ranks it second-most influential (after Reddit for ChatGPT) because it gets cited faster and you control how your product and competitors are described.
Treat other people's websites (blogs, PR, reviews) as the third cluster — the source constantly switches between second and third, so don't over-invest in one.
Lower priority: YouTube, then LinkedIn (LinkedIn citation behavior is currently thin and unpredictable; both posts and articles have been seen indexed, with no clear engagement pattern).
To track retention, log citations manually in a spreadsheet: record what got cited, from where, and monitor citation share over time to spot declines.
Plan content refresh cycles around observed citation decay — the source suspects a citation 'half-life' but has not measured it.
caveats: No off-the-shelf tool yet tracks citation half-life; source tracks manually.
Ranking positions 2 vs 3 are said to fluctuate.
LinkedIn/YouTube indexing patterns are described as early and patternless.
cards.source_name: The Head of Growth at a $100M Company Explains AEO.docx

cards.title: Exploit adjacent-surface indexing: Medium and Quora as Reddit exhaust valves
cards.summary: When Reddit is saturated, extend AEO content into Medium, Quora, and Substack, which are cited but less contested.
cards.use_when: Scaling AEO reach after you've established a Reddit and own-site presence and need additional citable surfaces.
steps: Prioritize Medium and Quora after Reddit and your own site — the source reports both are getting indexed/cited, with Quora still important though it 'got left behind' relative to earlier years.
Consider Substack cautiously: it is indexed, but journalists/authors there tend to gate content, which reduces citation pickup.
Anticipate new surfaces: X is not observed getting indexed by LLMs despite appearing in Google search results (the source hadn't seen it and planned to re-check); do not count on X for AEO today.

Watch LinkedIn and Instagram as likely next surfaces (6-12 month horizon per source) because both generate user content with reputation signals (likes, comments) similar to Reddit, unlike Discord which lacks structured reputation.
Verify each platform's current indexing behavior before committing budget — this landscape shifts within months.
caveats: All indexing observations are the source's informal tracking, not platform-confirmed.
Instagram/LinkedIn predictions are explicitly speculative bets.
cards.source_name: The Head of Growth at a $100M Company Explains AEO.docx

cards.title: Understand retrieval vs memorization to choose content tactics
cards.summary: LLMs either retrieve fresh web content (~60% of ChatGPT queries per the source) or answer from trained-in knowledge (~40%), and each mode needs different AEO tactics.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to invest in fresh web content or in seeding training-data surfaces, given that the two modes respond to different inputs.
steps: Treat Reddit interventions primarily as training-data plays: the cited material surfaces as trained-in knowledge and the click-through goes to Reddit, not you.
Treat third-party blogs and your own blog as retrieval/citation plays that can be fetched and surfaced with a link to your ecosystem.

Factor in logged-in memory: most real users are logged in to ChatGPT/Claude/Google, so what a model previously referenced for that user biases what it references next — first-mover citation can compound for that user.
Launch early to exploit first-mover advantage: showing up in a user's early queries can load into their memory and cause re-surfacing later.

For product changes (e.g., new model rollouts to free users), anticipate traffic shifts: source saw a ChatGPT click-through jump after a version rollout, hypothesizing increased memory, with traffic arriving from newly released regions.
caveats: The 60/40 retrieval/memorization split is a study cited by the source, not verified here.
Memory and retrieval mechanics are described as a black box that may change without notice.
cards.source_name: The Head of Growth at a $100M Company Explains AEO.docx

cards.title: Manufacture product-virality like the 'made with' watermark (PLG loop)
cards.summary: Building a recognizable maker's mark into every output drives organic, compounding acquisition; the source cites 'made with Gamma' and Calendly's 'powered by Calendly' as examples.
cards.use_when: Designing shareable outputs (presentations, invoices, order confirmations, gift cards, packaging inserts) that could carry your brand to new buyers.
steps: Identify every artifact your product sends to or creates for a non-user: emails, exports, embeds, PDFs, receipts, packaging.
Attach a lightweight, non-intrusive brand credit or footer to those artifacts ('Made with X').
Ensure the credit isn't so intrusive it degrades the customer's experience or gets removed by users; balance visibility with usefulness.
Watch for organic adoption where users cite the tool itself, then amplify the loop in marketing.
Use direct outbound tracking (self-reported 'how did you hear') to catch viral, non-click contributions that analytics miss.
caveats: Calendly revenue figures cited by the source as an example are illustrative, not a promise; verify firsthand.
Watermark strategy depends on product type — not all outputs are shareable.
cards.source_name: The Head of Growth at a $100M Company Explains AEO.docx

cards.title: Use JSON/schema incentives and future agentic placement (emerging play)
cards.summary: The source flags 'agentic bribing' — embedding incentives inside developer-tool JSON schemas or install packages — as a cutting-edge, speculative tactic for autonomous agents.
cards.use_when: Evaluating whether to experiment with agent-facing metadata or package incentives to influence AI agents choosing between tools.
steps: Understand the concept as described: hiding text or rewards inside a developer tool's JSON schema or install package to nudge an autonomous agent toward selecting your product.
Treat it as emerging and unproven; the source presents it as a futuristic frontier, not a validated channel.
If you test it, keep it within platform terms and your product's legitimate configuration metadata; the source itself notes it feels like gaming and expects platforms to close such loopholes.
Prefer durable mechanisms (MCP presence, integrations, open ecosystem) over manipulation that will be patched.
Track whether agentic commerce standards emerge — if they do, positioning your product as the default choice in agent flows could matter as much as current citation tactics.
caveats: This is described as a cutting-edge concept, not a tested procedure; no results are reported.
Manipulative incentivization may violate platform policies and invite penalties; source sees AEO advantages as temporary game-theory windows.
cards.source_name: The Head of Growth at a $100M Company Explains AEO.docx
